question: Smrtiaca kliatba Avada Kedavra podľa J. K. Rowlingovej súvisí so slovom, ktoré pozná každé dieťa z vystúpení kúzelníkov. O aké slovo ide?
source_excerpt: Avada Kedavra is an ancient spell in Aramaic, the original of abracadabra, which means 'let the thing be destroyed'.

extra.why_interesting: The most feared curse in the books sounds invented. It is actually a sinister twin of the harmless word every child hears at a stage magic show, and the sound gives players a real path to the answer.
extra.verification_notes: Rowling said at the 2004 Edinburgh Book Festival that Avada Kedavra is the Aramaic original of abracadabra (https://www.todaytranslations.com/news/ten-harry-potter-spells-translated-into-english); I found no newer development that changes this.

explanation: Rowlingová povedala, že ide o starú aramejskú formulu, z ktorej vzniklo „abrakadabra“. V jej verzii však znamená zhruba „nech je to zničené“, takže z nevinného kúzelníckeho slova sa stala vražedná kliatba.

question: Anglický názov fakulty Bystrohlav je Ravenclaw a skrýva sa v ňom slovo havran. Aké zviera je však podľa kníh J. K. Rowlingovej na erbe tejto fakulty?

extra.why_interesting: Players assume a house called 'Raven-claw' must have a raven on its crest; the books actually use an eagle, and many fans only know the raven from the films.
extra.verification_notes: The books and the official Wizarding World site give Ravenclaw an eagle (the films used a raven), and the new HBO series also returned to the eagle; see https://www.harrypotter.com/house/ravenclaw

explanation: V knihách má Bystrohlav na erbe orla a do klubovne sa vchádza cez dvere s klopadlom v tvare orla. Havrana z neho urobili až filmy.
